purpose: Adapt pinned EZ-Tree geometry into a tested Atlas GLB pair with physical cards, named materials, metric bark UVs and deterministic wind attributes.

artDirection.summary: Measure believable broadleaf branching and canopy shape at matched 10, 16 and 22 metre heights. Preserve physical leaf-card dimensions and inspect source normals rather than silently correcting the reference.

visual: Compare actual reference and Atlas shapes at matched height, camera, light and material conditions
Record source normal defects and every adapter override; no reference is accepted from topology counts alone
technical: Exact Atlas two-material/four-PNG graph retained between LODs
All eight required Float32 vertex attributes and finite MikkTSpace tangents
LOD0 at most18000 triangles, LOD1 at most5000 triangles
Retained leaves keep 1.2m card dimensions, pivot, UV tile and wind across LODs
Repeat outputs byte-identical under recorded toolchain; input files unchanged
runtime: Actual Atlas loader accepts pair and shares material images
Date replay gives deterministic wind at universe endpoints
Browser review measures LOD coverage rather than equating triangle budget with visual acceptance

provenance.prompt: Convert the fixed 16m Oak reference to an Atlas GLB pair, preserving physical leaves, canonical attachment pivots and the source Atlas texture bytes.

license.attribution: EZ-Tree geometry: Daniel Greenheck (MIT). Atlas textures and material graph: original project authoring v7.
restrictions: Retain upstream MIT notice; geometry comparison does not include any upstream photographs or textures

provenance.notes: Development candidate only, not a packaged asset. Upstream MIT notice preserved in tools/assetctl/vendor/ez-tree/LICENSE. Original Atlas texture license state remains NOASSERTION; no external textures imported.

experiments.selectionMetric: Canopy shape, repeatability, physical dimensions, LOD continuity and adaptation effort
